senses.definition: to choose not to do or have something, especially something enjoyable
senses.example: She abstained from sweets for the whole of Lent.

senses.definition: feeling resentment at having been treated unfairly
senses.example: The aggrieved tenants took their complaint to the city council.

senses.definition: a person who tells short, entertaining stories about real incidents
senses.example: An accomplished anecdotalist, he kept the whole table laughing.

senses.definition: connected with something else, often as a result or a part of it
senses.example: The lecture covered smoking and its associated risks.

senses.definition: to make up for a wrong or a sin
senses.example: He spent years trying to atone for his betrayal.

senses.definition: poetry of poor quality, clumsy in its rhythm or rhymes
senses.example: The greeting card was filled with bad verse about kittens.

senses.definition: to use or give something only in small amounts
senses.example: Be sparing with the salt, as the sauce is already rich.

senses.definition: to stiffen and lose the ability to bend or change
senses.example: Over the decades the club's rules had become rigid.

senses.definition: too great or intense to be described
senses.example: The view from the summit was beautiful beyond words.

senses.definition: to talk with too much pride about what one has or has done
senses.example: He never missed a chance to boast about his new car.

senses.definition: to behave in an excessively humble and obedient way toward someone
senses.example: The staff would bow and scrape whenever the owner visited.

senses.definition: to speak too proudly about one's achievements or possessions
senses.example: She liked to brag about her children's grades.

senses.definition: to fail to do what one has promised
senses.example: Having made the promise, he refused to break his word.

senses.definition: to make up for a loss, a wrong or a shortcoming
senses.example: No apology could compensate for the damage done.

senses.definition: to act in accordance with a rule, request or order
senses.example: All new buildings must comply with the fire code.

senses.definition: torn between opposing feelings or loyalties
senses.example: She felt conflicted about leaving her hometown.

senses.definition: made as an imitation of something else; not original
senses.example: The novel's plot felt copied rather than invented.

senses.definition: to be a disadvantage to someone or something
senses.example: His lack of experience may count against him.

senses.definition: a job that is easy and comfortable, and often well paid
senses.example: He landed a cushy job at his uncle's firm.

senses.definition: becoming smaller, weaker or worse over time
senses.example: The town's declining population worried the council.

senses.definition: made less sensitive or responsive to something through repeated exposure to it
senses.example: Years of violent films had left him desensitized.

senses.definition: not alike; distinct from one another
senses.example: The witnesses gave differing accounts of the accident.

senses.definition: to have or express an unfavorable opinion of something
senses.example: Her parents disapprove of her late nights.

senses.definition: to cause people to become distant or hostile toward each other
senses.example: Small quarrels can drive apart even the closest friends.

senses.definition: (informal) a job or task that is easy and undemanding
senses.example: Guarding the empty warehouse was an easy number.

senses.definition: (of a volcano) actively throwing out lava, ash or gases
senses.example: Tourists watched the erupting volcano from a safe distance.

senses.definition: able to be avoided or got away from
senses.example: The crisis was escapable, had anyone heeded the warnings.

senses.definition: giving reasons that make a fault seem less serious
senses.example: The judge found no excusing circumstances in the case.

senses.definition: relating to a group within a larger body that is at odds with the rest of it
senses.example: Factional disputes split the party before the election.

senses.definition: having a wide range of effects or influence
senses.example: The new law will have far-reaching consequences.

senses.definition: to flatter someone and seek their favor in a servile way
senses.example: The courtiers would fawn on the king to win his favor.

senses.definition: to pretend to be sick
senses.example: He would feign illness to get out of gym class.

senses.definition: having enough money and assets to meet one's obligations
senses.example: Only financially sound banks were allowed to bid.

senses.definition: lying with one's back on the ground or on a bed
senses.example: After the fall he lay flat on his back for an hour.

senses.definition: to grant someone the right to vote in elections
senses.example: The amendment would give the vote to eighteen-year-olds.

senses.definition: to look at something briefly or quickly
senses.example: She only had time to glance at the headlines.

senses.definition: used to something through long or repeated exposure to it
senses.example: Habituated to the noise of the city, he could sleep anywhere.

senses.definition: to have a strong, often restless desire for something
senses.example: Many retirees hanker after the routine of work.

senses.definition: a fortunate event that happens by chance
senses.example: The discovery of penicillin was a happy accident.

senses.definition: difficult to define, locate or get a firm answer from
senses.example: The exact cause of the outage was hard to pin down.

senses.definition: a person who dislikes people in general
senses.example: The novel's narrator is a bitter hater of humankind.

senses.definition: lacking insight or understanding; slow to notice things
senses.example: An imperceptive reader might miss the irony entirely.

senses.definition: suggested without being directly expressed
senses.example: There was an implied threat in his polite words.

senses.definition: having more money than one owes; making a profit
senses.example: After two difficult years, the company is back in the black.

senses.definition: to allow oneself to enjoy something, especially something one should perhaps avoid
senses.example: On holidays they indulge in long, lazy breakfasts.

senses.definition: remarks or actions that are rude and offensive
senses.example: The crowd shouted insults at the referee.

senses.definition: (of a plant or animal) brought into a region from elsewhere by people
senses.example: Introduced species such as rabbits have damaged the island's plants.

senses.definition: concerned only with one's own group or affairs, and uninterested in others
senses.example: The village had grown inward-looking and suspicious of strangers.

senses.definition: not serious; full of jokes
senses.example: His jokey manner hid a sharp mind.

senses.definition: giving reasons that show an action to be reasonable
senses.example: The lawyer presented several justifying circumstances.

senses.definition: the worst or least successful moment of something
senses.example: Losing the final was the low point of her career.

senses.definition: to do something to make up for a wrong one has done
senses.example: He bought her flowers to make amends for forgetting her birthday.

senses.definition: a wrong or inaccurate name or label
senses.example: Calling the whale a fish is a misdesignation.

senses.definition: making something, such as guilt or harm, less severe
senses.example: The court considered his youth a mitigating factor.

senses.definition: adding moisture to the skin to keep it soft
senses.example: She rubbed a moisturizing cream into her hands.

senses.definition: a word that has only recently come into use
senses.example: Every year the dictionary adds hundreds of new words.

senses.definition: fussy about small, unimportant details
senses.example: The editor's nitpicking comments filled the margins.

senses.definition: not letting light pass through; impossible to see through
senses.example: The bottle was made of nontransparent glass.

senses.definition: showing fine distinctions in meaning, feeling or expression
senses.example: The actor gave a nuanced performance as the aging king.

senses.definition: willingness to consider new ideas and opinions different from one's own
senses.example: Travel taught him an open-mindedness he had lacked.

senses.definition: performed in an exaggerated, unnatural way
senses.example: The villain's overacted death scene drew laughs.

senses.definition: intended to calm someone's anger or distress
senses.example: She spoke in a pacifying tone to the angry customer.

senses.definition: intended to end a quarrel or bring about peace
senses.example: The envoy made peacemaking gestures to both sides.

senses.definition: allowed by law, rules or custom
senses.example: Smoking is not permitted anywhere in the building.

senses.definition: (informal) something one finds especially annoying
senses.example: Loud chewing is my pet hate.

senses.definition: to put things next to each other, especially to compare or contrast them
senses.example: When you place side by side the two drafts, the changes are obvious.

senses.definition: a mild or courteous word used in place of a blunter one
senses.example: "Passed away" is a polite term for "died."

senses.definition: putting off things that should be done
senses.example: The procrastinating student started his essay the night before it was due.

senses.definition: a medicine or treatment sold with false claims that it works
senses.example: He wasted his savings on a quack remedy for baldness.

senses.definition: arguing about small, unimportant points
senses.example: Their endless quibbling delayed the agreement.

senses.definition: to read something carefully and in detail
senses.example: Lawyers read closely every clause of the contract.

senses.definition: practiced or prepared in advance rather than spontaneous
senses.example: His apology sounded rehearsed.

senses.definition: the committing of another crime after being punished for an earlier one
senses.example: Education programs in prisons have lowered rates of reoffending.

senses.definition: generally believed or said to be so
senses.example: The castle is the reputed birthplace of the king.

senses.definition: having had as much of something as one wants, or more
senses.example: Sated after the feast, the guests dozed by the fire.

senses.definition: to speak about something with mockery and contempt
senses.example: Critics scoff at the idea that the plan could work.

senses.definition: unwilling to change one's habits or opinions
senses.example: My grandfather is too set in his ways to try new food.

senses.definition: to correct someone's mistaken belief
senses.example: She was quick to set straight anyone who got her name wrong.

senses.definition: causing drowsiness or sleep
senses.example: The lecturer's monotone was sleep-inducing.

senses.definition: a little of something
senses.example: Add a small amount of water to thin the paint.

senses.definition: speaking in a persuasive, polished way that may hide insincerity
senses.example: A smooth-talking salesman convinced them to buy the car.

senses.definition: a job that requires little effort
senses.example: He had a soft job in the records office.

senses.definition: argument that seems sound at first but is actually false
senses.example: The pamphlet's specious reasoning fooled many readers.

senses.definition: to argue about very small, unimportant differences
senses.example: Let's not split hairs over a few cents.

senses.definition: to resist or confront someone more powerful with courage
senses.example: She was the only one who dared to stand up to the bully.

senses.definition: to flatter and obey someone powerful in order to win favor
senses.example: He refused to toady to the new manager.

senses.definition: not disturbed or thrown off balance by something
senses.example: Unfazed by the heckling, the speaker carried on.

senses.definition: a cure believed to work for every illness or problem
senses.example: Exercise is often praised as a universal remedy.

senses.definition: not based on reason or careful thought
senses.example: Their unreasoned fear of change held the company back.

senses.definition: to free someone from chains or from restrictions
senses.example: The reforms aimed to unshackle small businesses from red tape.

senses.definition: not able to be kept up or continued at its current level
senses.example: The company's rapid spending was unsustainable.

senses.definition: a mixture of good and bad experiences
senses.example: Every marriage has its ups and downs.

senses.definition: justified by the circumstances; deserved
senses.example: Given the risks, his caution was warranted.

senses.definition: to become gradually thinner and weaker, especially through illness
senses.example: Without exercise, muscles slowly waste away.

senses.definition: complaining in a high, irritating, self-pitying way
senses.example: The whining child wanted another ice cream.

senses.definition: to have an effect that hinders or harms someone or something
senses.example: His temper may work against him in the interview.

senses.definition: a name that is incorrect or misleading
senses.example: "Koala bear" is a wrong name, since the koala is not a bear.

senses.definition: a word used by mistake in place of the intended one
senses.example: In his nervousness he kept choosing the wrong word.
